newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign banks in Shanghai say yuan supply lacking.
newsitem.headline: Foreign banks in Shanghai say yuan supply lacking.

text.p: Two foreign banks which began local currency operations in Shanghai a month ago have said lack of yuan funds is limiting their business, the official China Daily Business Weekly reported on Sunday.
China has approved nine foreign banks to conduct yuan business in Shanghai's Pudong development zone.

Industrial Bank of Japan general manager Kiyoshige Akamatsu was quoted as saying demand for yuan was 10 times the amount of local currency the bank had available and he hoped to attract more yuan deposits from foreign-funded enterprises.
Overseas banks approved to do yuan business are limited to providing services to foreign-funded companies registered in Shanghai.

A Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp official was quoted in the report as saying the bank planned to grant its first yuan loan by the end of April after concluding loan agreements in principle with four companies.
The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi earlier this month became the first foreign bank to participate in a joint yuan loan with a Chinese bank to a foreign-funded joint venture.
